title.narrative: Leading from The South (2021-2025) - Grant Making

description.narrative: Primary target group: Small, medium, and large southern women´s rights organisations (SWROs) working at grassroot, national, sub-regional and regional and global levels, on thehuman rights of women, girls and trans people to advocate for the full achievement of gender equalityand other human rights in the Global South.Secondary Target Group: Pacific Women's Fund

Women's Fund Asia funds Asia-based activists and groups that are committed to the application of the feministrights-based approach in their pursuit of progressive realisation of their rights. The grants focus onfilling the gaps faced by women, girls, trans, and intersex groups and these grants aim at beingflexible. The key features of our grant-making strategy are:a. Multi-Level: We support a wide range of feminist organisations and networks working atgrassroot, national, sub-regional and regional and global levels. Accordingly, these groupsalso have diverse budgets, operations and outreach (small, medium and large).b. Flexible: In order to ensure maximum outreach, WFA’s grant-making is flexible in terms oftypes of grant structures it supports – from individuals to groups to networks toconsortiums.

All grants provided by us is through an open call for proposals. The call for proposals are open only in 2021 and 2022 for a fixed duration. The grant call for 2021 runs from 2021-2024 and the grant call for 2022 runs from 2022-2025.
All targets have been met fully.

The LFS Cycle 2 (2022) supported 40 groups (from all regions supported by WFA). However, in total only 18 of the 40 groups received the 1st instalment of their funds in 2022. The remaining 22 groups supported under LFS Cycle 2 will be reported in the next report. In addition, 1 grantee partner from LFS Cycle 1 (2021) received the first instalment of their funds in early 2022, thus the calculations for the 2022 reporting period also includes this group, bringing the total to 19 groups supported under the LFS 2022 cycle and 5 groups were supported under the Kaagapay Fund.

The LFS Cycle 2 (2022) supported 42 groups (from all regions supported by WFA. 2 additional groups are supported in 2023). However, in total only 18 of the 42 groups received the 1st instalment of their funds in 2022. The remaining 22 groups supported under LFS Cycle 2 received disbursement in 2023.
